rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited account has the Prophet declare Zayd his son with reciprocal inheritance, which is why Zayd was called Muhammad’s son.
rows.anchor: اشهدوا أن زيدا ابني أرثه ويرثني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Zayd married Zaynab; after the Prophet saw her and felt drawn to her, Zayd offered to divorce her, but the Prophet told him to keep his wife and fear God.
rows.anchor: اذهب واتق الله وامسك عليك زوجك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says God then married Zaynab to the Prophet, after which hypocrites objected that he prohibited sons’ wives yet married his adopted son’s former wife.
rows.anchor: فقال المنافقون يحرم علينا نساء أبنائنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ibn Mardawayh, is said to transmit a similar account with some differences.
rows.anchor: في الدر المنثور عن ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet saying he has greater claim over every believer than the believer himself; the Prophet assumes debts left by the dead, while heirs receive their property.
rows.anchor: عن جابر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه كان يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes other reports with the same meaning from both Shi‘i and Sunni routes.
rows.anchor: وفي معناه روايات أخر من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Burayda’s account says that after he criticized Ali on returning from Yemen, the Prophet asked whether he had greater claim over believers and declared Ali the mawla of whoever had the Prophet as mawla.
rows.anchor: ألست أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم؟ قلت بلى يا رسول الله. قال من كنت مولاه فعلي مولاه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report from Abdullah ibn Ja‘far, the Prophet says he has greater claim over believers than themselves and that Ali has that same claim over whoever the Prophet has it over.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول أنا أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The author says al-Kafi transmits the same report through Ja‘far and that reports of this meaning from both communities are innumerable.
rows.anchor: ورواه في الكافي بإسناده عن جعفر عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والأحاديث في هذا المعنى من طرق الفريقين

words: إِلَّآ أَن تَفْعَلُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَوْلِيَآئِكُم مَّعْرُوفًۭا
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Asked what inheritance the mawali receive, Imam al-Sadiq answers that they inherit only as stated in the exception allowing kindness to one’s allies.
rows.anchor: ليس لهم من الميراث إلا ما قال الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when asked when the Prophet’s covenant was taken, the Prophet answered that it was while Adam was between spirit and body.
rows.anchor: قيل يا رسول الله متى أخذ ميثاقك؟ قال وآدم بين الروح والجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba’i explains the covenant report as referring to a mode of existence before this present worldly existence.
rows.anchor: ومعناه كون الميثاق مأخوذا في نشأة غير هذه النشأة وقبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on lingering after meals is explained by the guests’ presence hurting the Prophet and his shyness about asking them to leave; God’s lack of shyness means he states the truth and teaches proper etiquette.
rows.anchor: لا تمكثوا كذلك لأن مكثكم ذلك كان يتأذى منه النبي فيستحيي منكم أن يسألكم الخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking the Prophet’s wives for an item is a euphemism for speaking with them when a need arises; the speech must take place from behind a screen.
rows.anchor: وسؤالهن متاعا كناية عن تكليمهن لحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The screen rule serves the stated interest of purifying the hearts of both the men and the Prophet’s wives.
rows.anchor: ذلكم أطهر لقلوبكم وقلوبهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception to the screen rule includes the wives’ fathers, sons, brothers, nephews through brothers and sisters, their women, and those owned by them; these male relatives are unmarriageable kin.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء محارم، قيل ولم يذكر الأعمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported explanation for omitting paternal and maternal uncles is that they might describe the women to their sons.
rows.anchor: قيل ولم يذكر الأعمام والأخوال لأنهم من الممكن أن يصفوهن لأبنائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive phrase for the women suggests that it means believing women, as in the parallel wording in 24:31.
rows.anchor: وإضافة النساء إلى ضميرهن يلوح إلى أن المراد النساء المؤمنات دون الكوافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God reinforces the rule, especially through the shift from third-person reference to direct address.
rows.anchor: فيه تأكيد الحكم وخاصة من جهة الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of prayer is inclination or turning toward someone; God’s prayer for the Prophet is an unrestricted bestowal of mercy.
rows.anchor: أصل الصلاة الانعطاف فصلاته تعالى انعطافه عليه بالرحمة انعطافا مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ prayer for the Prophet is their turning toward him through praise and seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وكذلك صلاة الملائكة عليه انعطاف عليه بالتزكية والاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers’ prayer for the Prophet means supplication for mercy.
rows.anchor: وهي من المؤمنين الدعاء بالرحمة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama says the Prophet ruled that divorce cannot precede marriage and manumission cannot precede ownership; similar reports are attributed to Jabir and Aisha.
rows.anchor: عن المسور بن مخرمة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Asked how many women were made lawful to the Prophet, Abu Ja‘far answers that he could marry as many as he wished.
rows.anchor: عن الحضرمي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The Prophet could marry his paternal and maternal cousins and the wives who migrated with him; he could also accept a believing woman’s gift of herself without a dowry, a privilege unavailable to other men, who require a dowry.
rows.anchor: عن الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn identifies the woman who gifted herself to the Prophet as Umm Sharik al-Azdiyya.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports name the woman as Khawla bint al-Hakim, Layla bint al-Khatim, or Maymuna; al-Tabataba’i concludes that several women apparently offered themselves.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الواهبة نفسها عدة من النساء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far recounts an Ansari widow offering herself, Hafsa insulting her, and the Prophet defending her and promising God’s reward; the report says revelation then made self-gifting lawful exclusively for him.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله كفي عنها يا حفصة فإنها خير منك رغبت في رسول الله ولمتها وعبتها

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report says Aisha objected that women were offering themselves without dowries and remarked that God seemed to hasten to satisfy the Prophet’s desire.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة ما بال النساء يبذلن أنفسهن بلا مهر؟

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In the same report, the Prophet answers Aisha that if she obeys God, God will hasten to satisfy her desire.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فإنك إن أطعت الله سارع في هواك

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq interpret deferring a wife as not marrying her, and accommodating one as marrying her.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام من أرجى لم ينكح ومن آوى فقد نكح

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far says the ban on further women means women prohibited by 4:23; the Prophet could otherwise marry any woman except those forbidden there, contrary to the claim that ordinary men could replace wives at will while he could not.
rows.anchor: عن الحضرمي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to say that God restricted the Prophet to the nine wives he died leaving.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn rejects the nine-wife restriction, saying the Prophet could have married women beyond those wives.
rows.anchor: فأخبرت علي بن الحسين فقال لو شاء تزوج غيرهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qummi’s account says the Prophet’s companions lingered after eating at his wedding feast for Zaynab, while he wanted privacy with her; they had entered without permission, so the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: كان يحب أن يخلو مع زينب فأنزل الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says detailed versions of the wedding-feast story are transmitted through Anas by various routes.
rows.anchor: وروي تفصيل القصة عن أنس بطرق مختلفة

rows.speaker: صالح بن كيسان
rows.claim: Salih ibn Kaysan dates the revelation of the screen rule for the Prophet’s wives to Dhu al-Qi‘dah in year five after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: عن صالح بن كيسان قال نزل حجاب رسول الله على نسائه في ذي القعدة سنة خمس من الهجرة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas is also reported to place the revelation in the year the Prophet consummated his marriage to Zaynab.
rows.anchor: ورواها أيضا ابن سعد عن أنس وفيه أن السنة كانت

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that Talha ibn Ubayd Allah said the men were barred from the Prophet’s female cousins while he could marry their wives after his death; the verse followed.
rows.anchor: عن السدي قال بلغنا أن طلحة بن عبيد الله قال أيحجبنا محمد عن بنات عمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported explanation says Gabriel’s descent after the interruption in revelation frightened the angels, who thought the Hour had come; after the fear passed, they asked what God had said and were told the revelation was the truth. The author rejects it as an adequate explanation.
rows.anchor: أن الله لما بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بعد فترة بينه وبين عيسى عليهما السلام لم ينزل فيها شيء من الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported explanation makes the pronoun refer to angels who faint or prostrate when revelation reaches one angel; they then ask what their Lord said. The author says neither account adequately interprets the verse.
rows.anchor: أن الضمير للملائكة والمراد أن الله سبحانه إذا أوحى إلى بعض الملائكة غشي على الملائكة عند سماع الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about provision challenges the polytheists’ reliance on gods to satisfy them and expand their livelihood: provision is created, and even they recognize that only God creates it, though they will not admit it aloud.
rows.anchor: احتجاج آخر على المشركين من جهة الرزق الذي هو الملاك العمدة في اتخاذهم الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the opponents will not confess the answer aloud despite inwardly acknowledging it, the Prophet is instructed to answer on their behalf: God provides.
rows.anchor: لكنهم يستنكفون عن الاعتراف به بألسنتهم وإن أذعنت به قلوبهم ولذلك أمر أن ينوبهم في الجواب

words: وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After decisive proof, the Prophet frames the disagreement fairly: one side must be guided and the other clearly astray, so the hearers should judge the evidence and distinguish truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول بعد إلقاء الحجة القاطعة ووضوح الحق في مسألة الألوهية مبني على سلوك طريق الإنصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between being on guidance and being in error pictures the guided as elevated at a beacon overlooking the path, while the astray are immersed in darkness without knowing their direction.
rows.anchor: أن المهتدي كأنه مستعل على منار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person bears his own deeds, especially evil deeds, and their consequences do not pass to someone else; the two sides answer for their own actions.
rows.anchor: العمل وخاصة عمل الشر لا يتعدى عن عامله ولا يلحق وباله إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet calls his side’s actions crimes but describes the opponents’ actions neutrally as what they do, observing good manners in debate.
rows.anchor: أخذ بحسن الأدب في المناظرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement prepares for the next verse: because the sides differ in good and evil actions, they must be gathered and separated so each receives the reward or punishment due to it.
rows.anchor: وهذا تمهيد لما في الآية التالية من حديث الجمع والفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers everyone and then judges between them justly, distinguishing the good-doer from the wrongdoer; this establishes resurrection and makes judgment and recompense exclusive to God, undermining rival claims to lordship.
rows.anchor: فالآية تثبت البعث لتمييز المحسن من المسيء أولا ثم انحصار التمييز والجزاء في جانبه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fattah is a divine name; opening means making a useful division between two things, as when a door is opened or two things are distinguished in their essence, qualities, and acts.
rows.anchor: والفتاح من أسماء الله الحسنى والفتح إيجاد الفصل بين شيئين لفائدة تترتب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to show the alleged partners asks whether they possess the necessary qualities of a deity worthy of worship: independent life, knowledge, power, hearing, and sight.
rows.anchor: حتى يختبر هل فيهم الصفات الضرورية للإله المستحق للعبادة من الاستقلال بالحياة والعلم والقدرة والسمع والبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols are dead and lack knowledge and power; if the alleged partners are angels or other beings represented by idols, their perfections and derived acts come from God, so they have no independent share in his infinite perfection or governance.
rows.anchor: وهم وإن لم يخلوا عن حياة وعلم وقدرة إلا أن ما لهم من صفات الكمال مفاضة عليهم من الله سبحانه لا استقلال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night enters the day by shortening the day as the night grows longer, and the day enters the night by shortening the night as the day grows longer; this ongoing seasonal change is intended.
rows.anchor: إيلاج الليل في النهار قصر النهار بطول الليل وإيلاج النهار في الليل قصر الليل بطول النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for interpenetration signals continual change in day and night, unlike the sun and moon’s fixed course; the wording about their subjection is figurative and accommodating.
rows.anchor: الدال على استمرار التغيير بخلاف جريان الشمس والقمر فإنه ثابت على حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s creation and management of humans, land, sea, earth, and sky lead to the conclusion that he is Lord and owns all things; the ownership statement prepares for the denial that other beings own anything.
rows.anchor: إذا كان أمر خلقكم وتدبيركم برا وبحرا وأرضا وسماء منتسبا إليه مدبرا بتدبيره

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines qitmir as the trace or mark at the top of a date stone, a model for something very small.
rows.anchor: القطمير على ما قاله الراغب الأثر على رأس النواة وذلك مثل للشيء الطفيف

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majma‘ defines qitmir as the thin wrapper or skin around a date stone.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع القطمير لفافة النواة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported definition of qitmir is the kernel inside the date stone.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحبة في بطن النواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever definition is chosen, qitmir serves as an emphatic image for denying even the slightest ownership to those invoked besides God.
rows.anchor: والكلام على أي حال مبالغة في نفي أصل الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God are the worshippers’ gods, including idols and the beings believed to stand behind them.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالذين تدعون من دون الله آلهتهم الذين كانوا يدعونها من الأصنام وأربابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot hear because they are insentient; their supposed lords, such as angels and holy human beings, are occupied with other matters and possess no independent hearing, hearing only when God enables it.
rows.anchor: لأن الأصنام جمادات لا شعور لها ولا حس وأرباب الأصنام كالملائكة والقديسين من البشر في شغل شاغل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited passage says Christ and the proximate angels do not disdain being servants of God; those who scorn worship will be gathered to him, supporting the dependence of alleged divine partners.
rows.anchor: لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection the alleged partners disown the worship and shirk directed to them instead of acting as intercessors, as in the disavowal described in 2:166.
rows.anchor: أي يردون عبادتكم إليكم ويتبرؤون منكم بدلا من أن يكونوا شفعاء لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s denial that the invoked answer and its account of their later rejection correspond to the parallel passage the author cites from al-Ahqaf.
rows.anchor: فالآية في نفي الاستجابة وكفر الشركاء يوم القيامة في معنى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding address may be specifically to the Prophet after turning away from opponents who do not understand, or may use a particular address to mean any listener.
rows.anchor: وهو خطاب خاص بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بعد الإعراض عن خطابهم لعدم تفقههم بالبيان الحق أو خطاب عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares this address to similar second-person forms in 18:17–18.
rows.anchor: في صورة الخطاب الخاص خوطب به السامع أي من كان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Imam al-Sadiq says that before resurrection God sends rain on the earth for forty mornings, bringing bones together and growing flesh; the author notes other reports with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إذا أراد الله أن يبعث الخلق أمطر السماء على الأرض أربعين صباحا فاجتمعت الأوصال ونبتت اللحوم

rows.speaker: أبو رزين العقيلي
rows.claim: Abu Ruzayn al-Uqayli reports asking the Prophet how God revives the dead; the Prophet compares it to seeing barren land become green and moving, saying resurrection is like that.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رزين العقيلي قال قلت يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report through Abu al-Jarud from Abu Ja‘far quotes the Prophet: every statement is confirmed or falsified by action; matching deeds raise a person’s words, while contradicting deeds cause the words to be rejected and the person cast into the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali, transmitting from his father, says God has regions in the heavens and that whoever ascends to one of them has ascended to God; he supports this with verses about the angels’ ascent, Jesus’ raising, and good words and deeds ascending.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن علي عن أبيه عليه السلام في حديث قال وإن لله تبارك وتعالى بقاعا في سماواته فمن عرج به إلى بقعة منها فقد عرج به إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that al-Faqih transmits a similar report.
rows.anchor: وعن الفقيه مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahj al-Balagha says the heavens’ acknowledgment of God’s lordship and obedience is why he made them the place of his Throne, abode of angels, and route for good words and deeds to ascend.
rows.anchor: ولولا إقرارهن له بالربوبية وإذعانهن له بالطواعية لما جعلهن موضعا لعرشه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far explains ajaj, describing the salty sea, as bitter.
rows.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far defines qitmir as the thin skin on the back of a date stone.
rows.anchor: قال الجلدة الرقيقة التي على ظهر النوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing that creation and governance belong to God and alleged gods own nothing, the passage adds a warning: God needs no people, while they need him, and he can replace them if he wills as recompense for their deeds.
rows.anchor: أخذ يبين ذلك ببيان آخر مشوب بالوعيد والتهديد وهو أنه تعالى غني عنهم وهم فقراء إليه فله أن يذهبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened destruction concerns deniers rather than believers who respond to the Prophet’s warning; he is a warner like earlier prophets, whose rejected warnings were followed by severe punishment of their peoples.
rows.anchor: هذه المؤاخذة والإهلاك لا يشمل إلا هؤلاء المكذبين دون المؤمنين الذين يؤثر فيهم إنذار النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers’ conduct suggests that they imagine they can become independent of God through idol worship and that God needs them; the verse refutes this by restricting all poverty to people and all richness to God.
rows.anchor: السياق يشعر بأن أعمال هؤلاء المكذبين كانت تكشف عن أنهم كانوا يتوهمون أن لهم أن يستغنوا عن الله سبحانه بعبادة آلهتهم

words: أَنتُمُ ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because richness and poverty mean possession and lack and cannot both be absent, the exclusive wording implies that people have only poverty while God has only richness.
rows.anchor: وإذ كان الغنى والفقر وهما الوجدان والفقدان متقابلين لا يرتفعان عن موضوعهما كان لازم القصر السابق قصر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is rich in himself and can dispense with or replace people, while they are inherently unable to dispense with him; his creation and management ground this asymmetry, and he is praised in those acts.
rows.anchor: والملاك في غناه تعالى عنهم وفقرهم أنه تعالى خالقهم ومدبر أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse addresses people, the universal cause—dependence on the creator and manager—extends the judgment to all creatures, whether people means deniers specifically or humankind generally.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن عموم علة الحكم يعمم الحكم فكأنه قيل أنتم معاشر الخليقة الفقراء إلى خالقكم المدبر لأمركم
